title: Emyr's Wiggle Words
markdown:
On a very drizzly, drippy sort of day, the clouds looked like fluffy sheep in the sky. Rain pattered a sleepy tune on the windowpanes. In a cozy cottage near the sea lived three good friends.

There was Tess, a seal. She was as slick and cheerful as a shiny black pebble. Her coat gleamed. Tess had a happy bark. It could make even a grumpy raindrop giggle. She loved splashing in puddles, but today she was happy to be warm and dry inside.

Then there was Freya, a panda. She was all soft and cuddly. Freya loved to watch raindrops race down the window. Her fur felt like the softest cloud. Her big dark eyes missed nothing. Freya liked things just right. She was very loyal to her friends. Today she traced patterns on the steamy glass with a fuzzy paw.

And, of course, there was Old Tom. He was the gardener. His hands smelled like sunshine and rich soil. His smile was as warm as a summer afternoon. He wore glasses with a smudge of dirt. But his eyes twinkled with kindness. Old Tom understood plants and animals. He always made his friends happy.

Old Tom loved his beautiful garden. Flowers sang to the sun. Bushes whispered secrets to the wind. One day the drizzle faded. A shy sun peeked through the clouds. Old Tom clapped his hands. “We shall have a garden concert,” he declared. “Music amongst the daisies and a symphony of sweet peas.”

Tess barked with delight. Her whole body wiggled. “Hooray. Music and flowers,” she flippered. She did a little bouncy dance on the rug.

Freya nodded. Her big eyes sparkled. “A concert would be simply lovely, Old Tom,” she said softly. She imagined gentle notes floating on the breeze. They would tickle the petals of the forget-me-nots.

Now, in those days, invitations to garden concerts were special treasures. They promised fun and friendship. And who wrote these invitations? Emyr the pony, of course. Emyr was a neat little fellow. His mane was like spun moonlight, soft and silvery. His trot was lighter than a dandelion seed dancing on the wind. He loved to help his friends. He loved to express himself through writing.

“I shall write the invitations,” Emyr announced. He swished his tail. He had a special goose-feather quill. He dipped it in ink. The ink smelled faintly of blueberries. He wrote with careful swirls and loops. Fancy flicks and curls. Everyone wondered if there was a secret code. It looked as if his pen was dancing on the page.

“But, Emyr,” said Freya. She tilted her head. Her soft ears twitched. “These look… very… wiggly.” She pointed to the first invitation.

Tess peered at the paper. Her whiskers twitched with curiosity. “It looks like a happy spaghetti noodle tried to dance,” she observed. A tiny giggle escaped her.

Emyr beamed. His chest puffed out. “That’s the beauty of it,” he explained. “Each curl is a special hello. Each loop is a little burst of joy. It’s my heart on paper.”

Tess and Freya looked at the invitations. They saw a delightful jumble of swooshes and squiggles.

“What does this one say?” Freya asked. She pointed to a twirly line doing a loop-de-loop.

Tess squinted. “Hmm, it looks like… Come to the… sparkly… rain puddle… by the big blue mushroom?”

“And this one?” Freya pointed to another that looked like a tiny whirlwind. “Bring your… very… long… stripey… socks?”

Oh dear. This was a puzzle. The concert was meant to be in Old Tom’s sunny garden. Not in a sparkly rain puddle. And the music would be played by friends. Not by stripey socks. Tess imagined a sock playing a violin. She giggled again.

Old Tom stepped forward. His voice was soft like moss. “Emyr has a very artistic way of writing. He puts his heart into every letter.” He patted Emyr’s mane. “But perhaps, for invitations, we need words everyone can understand. So no one misses the fun.”

Emyr’s ears drooped a little. He hadn’t meant to make things confusing. He just loved making his letters dance with happiness. He looked down at his hooves.

Freya had a little idea. She nudged Tess. Then she whispered to Old Tom. “Old Tom, could we ask Emyr to write his special swooshes, but maybe… a little straighter for the words? Just the words part, so everyone knows when and where?”

Old Tom chuckled. It was a warm sound like pebbles tumbling in a stream. “That’s a splendid idea, Freya.”

So Emyr tried again. He dipped his quill. He thought very hard about straight lines and clear words. Then out came another cascade of curls and loops. This time the loops were even bigger. The curls were so very curly, they seemed to be having a grand party. They danced around the words Emyr had tried to write straight.

Tess looked at the new invitations. “This one looks like a curly worm doing a spectacular somersault,” she giggled.

Freya sighed, a tiny soft sound. “It’s still very wiggly, Emyr. It’s like the letters are playing hide-and-seek.”

Emyr looked worried. He just wanted to make everyone happy. He wanted to share the joy of the concert. As he looked at the invitations with his head tilted, Old Tom said, “You know, Emyr, your writing is very special. It’s like a secret code of joy. What if we don’t try to make it perfectly straight at all? What if we let the joy show?”

Tess and Freya looked at Old Tom. Their eyes were wide with surprise. Then they looked at the invitations. They saw wild curls and joyful loops.

“You mean… people will understand?” asked Tess, her voice full of wonder.

“Well,” said Old Tom, his eyes twinkling behind his glasses, “they might not understand every single word right away. But they’ll understand the feeling. They’ll see the excitement in Emyr’s fancy swooshes. They’ll see the bright happy ink. And isn’t that what a concert is all about? Excitement and sharing joy?”

Emyr perked up. He looked at his wiggly curly invitations. For the first time he saw them with new eyes. They weren’t just confusing squiggles. They were a happy dance, a celebration. A little piece of Emyr’s own joyful heart, reaching out to his friends.

So the invitations were sent out. Each one was a masterpiece of curls and loops. Some looked like happy little waves rolling towards the shore. Others looked like tiny musical notes dancing in the breeze. The friends who received them peered at them, a little puzzled at first. But then they saw Old Tom’s name. They saw the date. And they could feel the excitement Emyr had poured into each one. They saw a loop that looked like a smile. A swirl that felt like a happy bounce. They knew it meant a party in the garden.

And on the day of the concert, the garden was alive with music. The sun shone brightly. It warmed the red petals of the roses. The air buzzed with happy melodies. Tess’s tail thumped a gentle rhythm on the soft grass. Freya swayed gently. Her eyes were closed, listening to the sweet sounds. The sweet scent of honeysuckle filled the air. And Old Tom beamed. He looked as bright as his favourite roses.

When Emyr arrived, trotting proudly, his moonlight mane gleaming, everyone cheered.

“Emyr,” they called out. Their voices were full of warmth. “Your invitations were wonderful. So unique and full of fun.”

Emyr felt a happy warmth spread through his mane, right down to his hooves. Then a gust of wind rustled through the garden. It threatened to blow away the leftover invitations Emyr had brought. Quickly, Emyr used his own silvery mane to hold them down. He didn’t mind that it got a little messy. He valued his art and sharing it more than his perfect mane.

The leftover invitations stayed put under the moonlight hair, still curly, still readable enough, and the concert went on among the daisies.
characters: Emyr (a moonlight-maned pony), Tess (a cheerful seal), Freya (a rain-watching panda)
